key_insight: Multiwavelength photoluminescence reveals that PEABF4 treatment initially reduces interfacial recombination but accelerates degradation during thermal aging, with losses extending into the perovskite absorber.
engineering_relevance: Depth-sensitive, nondestructive monitoring can help engineers assess whether interface passivation improves both initial performance and thermal durability.
method: Use multiple excitation wavelengths to probe depth-dependent photoluminescence responses.
Compare PEABF4-treated and untreated perovskite stacks during thermal aging.
Interpret PL decay signatures using diffusion–recombination simulations.
evidence_signal: PL measurements indicate reduced recombination from fullerene deposition after treatment, followed by faster degradation during thermal aging; simulations support contributions from changing surface recombination velocity and bulk lifetime.
watch_item: Depth-dependent losses are inferred through optical measurements and modeling; the abstract provides no quantitative lifetime gains or device-efficiency validation.
paper_title: Wavelength-Dependent Photoluminescence Mapping of Depth-Dependent Degradation Under Thermal Stress in Phenethylammonium Tetrafluoroborate Treated Perovskite Solar Cells
